```{r}
library(brms)      # The core Bayesian regression engine
library(tidyverse) # For data cleaning (dplyr) and basic plotting (ggplot2)
library(bayesplot) # For MCMC diagnostic plots
library(tidybayes) # For extracting and plotting Bayesian uncertainty
```

```{r}
dat <- na.omit(read.csv("data.csv"))
dim(dat)
```

# Fitting

```{r}
# Define a weak prior (Optional but recommended for Bayesian rigor)
# This tells the model: "Assume the effect of height and stems is normally distributed around 0, but allow it to be positive or negative based on data."
prr <- c(prior(normal(0, 10), class = "b"))

# Fit the Bayesian Linear Regression Model
soybean_model <- brm(
  formula = grain_yield ~ plant_height + number_of_stems,
  data = dat,
  family = gaussian(), # Assumes the target 'grain_yield' is continuous/normal
  prior = prr,
  chains = 4,          # Run 4 parallel simulations
  iter = 2000,         # 2000 steps per simulation
  warmup = 1000,       # Discard the first 1000 steps
  seed = 123           # For exact reproducibility
)
```

# Diagnostics

```{r}
# 1. Check R-hat values (Must be less than 1.05)
summary(soybean_model)

# 2. Check Trace Plots for "hairy caterpillar" mixing
mcmc_trace(soybean_model)
```

# Posterior Predictive Check

```{r}
# Plot the actual yield data (dark line) against 50 simulated yield datasets (light lines)
pp_check(soybean_model, ndraws = 50) +
  labs(title = "Posterior Predictive Check: Soybean Yield",
       subtitle = "Does the simulated data match the real data shape?")
```

# Visualization & Inference

```{r}
# 1. View the mathematical summaries and Credible Intervals
summary(soybean_model)

# 2. The Ultimate Visual: Conditional Effects
# This plots the isolated effect of plant height on yield, complete with Bayesian uncertainty bands
plot(conditional_effects(soybean_model), ask = FALSE)

# 3. Ridge Plot (Advanced Visualization)
# Shows the beautiful posterior distributions for your coefficients
mcmc_areas(soybean_model, 
           pars = c("b_plant_height", "b_number_of_stems"),
           prob = 0.95) +
  labs(title = "Posterior Distributions of Biological Predictors")
```
